Moments after matching Colin Montgomerie's record of season-long European tour titles on Sunday, the Northern Irishman was asked about the health of his father. An emotional McIlroy revealed Gerry has been in hospital for two months after "a huge operation" - a double lung transplant - at the end of September. "He's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy told the DP World Tour. "But before I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him. He said to me: 'Go win The Race to Dubai'. It came after a thrilling climax at the traditional season-ending DP World Tour Championship with Tyrrell Hatton securing a commanding victory, while McIlroy pipped Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra to the overall crown. Hatton's closing six-under-par 66 helped him romp to a five-shot victory on 15 under par but most eyes were on the thrilling battle that went down to the final hole. It is the fifth successive year that McIlroy has won the award and it has drawn him level with Montgomerie, the Scot who set a mark 21 years ago that few thought would ever be matched. "Yeah, double digits," smiled McIlroy when asked what would be his final target of Race to Dubai victories. "I'd love to surpass Monty next year and we'll go from there." McIlroy's confidence in going along with a target shouted out by the fans surrounding the 18th green at the Earth Course in Dubai on Sunday was refreshing to hear. But he appears to be playing and talking with a little more freedom in recent years - the sort of freedom that comes as a result of finally completing the career Grand Slam and winning successive Masters titles - and leads to declarations of winning 10, or more. "Winning eight Order of Merits (Race to Dubai titles) was never in my list of goals growing up," said McIlroy, who closed with a bogey-free 67 to finish on 10 under and must surely now be considered Europe's greatest golfer. 【BBC Sport】Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Kayla Harrison has won 20 of her 21 professional fights Kayla Harrison shocked returning great Amanda Nunes by submitting the former double champion to retain her bantamweight title at UFC 334 in New York. Nunes, 38, was fighting for the first time since she brought her glittering career to a close in 2023, after dominating at bantamweight and featherweight for years. Enticed by the challenge of fighting Harrison, the Brazilian came out of retirement for the bout but could not topple her friend and former training partner. Just 10 months after neck and spinal surgery, 36-year-old American Harrison ended the contest in the fourth round at Madison Square Garden with a rear-naked choke. Afterwards, Harrison reflected on the challenges she's overcome during her career. As a youngster, Harrison was sexually abused by her judo coach, who was sentenced to 10 years in prison after being found guilty. Harrison went on to become a two-time Olympic gold medallist in judo before moving into mixed martial arts where she became a two-time PFL lightweight world champion and then won UFC bantamweight gold in just her third fight in the organisation. "I was sexually abused at a young age, statistically I'm not supposed to be here," said Harrison. "If you'd told me at six years old this would be my life and at 16, I wouldn't have believed you. "I'm really grateful, humbled and it's an honour and privilege to stand before you." In the main event, heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Josh Hokit. In a gruelling contest which featured a record 383 significant strikes in a UFC heavyweight bout, Frenchman Gane's counter striking off the back foot proved the difference. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Harrison submitted Nunes with a rear-naked choke Nunes left the UFC in 2023 as the only woman to hold UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously, and the only fighter, male or female, to successfully defend both belts. During Nunes' remarkable run, she beat some of the greatest names in MMA history, such as Ronda Rousey, Cris Cyborg and Valentina Shevchenko, but it was the prospect of fighting Harrison which brought her out of retirement. The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, which Nunes left in 2022.
